name: india-reference-migration-v1
purpose: Design-only, machine-readable specification of the ten proposed P2 reference-data items. This record proposes definitions; it approves nothing, admits no data and authorizes no code change.

required_before_any_implementation: Separate owner approval of an explicit amendment that names this record
Rights determination and written authority for any proposed reference source
A new, separately approved fixture amendment if behavioural evidence is needed
An explicit, separately approved unfreeze decision for the named code path

gate_impact.statement: No gate status, release condition or freeze value is altered by this design-only record.

examples.note: Both examples are illustrative design inputs only and are explicitly NOT APPROVED. They do not grant rights, authorize collection or admit any data.

instrument_universe.contract_scope: current near-month monthly futures series only

reference_authority.name: NSE official historical reference archive
reference_authority.proposed_role: reference metadata and revision authority for the example universe

p2_items.title: Instrument identity across exchange/product/contract changes
p2_items.problem: A venue, product or contract reclassification must not silently create a second identity for the same economic instrument, nor merge two different ones.

proposed_model.stable_id_rule: Stable ID = versioned hash of canonical JSON of identity_key_fields; aliases carry effective_from_ns and effective_to_ns.
proposed_model.alias_table: old_id -> new_id with non-overlapping effective intervals

invariants: Exactly one canonical identity per instrument at any instant.
Every alias maps to a canonical identity with an explicit effective interval.
No identity is reassigned to a different economic instrument.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Replay of the example universe resolves each historical record to exactly one canonical ID.
Ambiguous or overlapping alias intervals fail closed.

p2_items.title: Listing, expiry, symbol-change and delisting lifecycle
p2_items.problem: Instrument state transitions must be point-in-time addressable and must not leave gaps or overlapping states.

proposed_model.interval_rule: States are half-open intervals [effective_from_ns, effective_to_ns) with no gaps or overlaps per instrument.

invariants: Exactly one lifecycle state per instrument at any instant.
Symbol changes preserve the stable ID and append an alias.
Terminal states cannot be silently reopened; a new listing requires a new identity.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Interval coverage is contiguous and non-overlapping across the example universe.
Lifecycle queries at boundary instants are deterministic.

p2_items.title: Corporate actions and adjustment history
p2_items.problem: Historical series must remain reproducible after splits, bonuses, dividends, mergers, spin-offs and rights issues.

proposed_model.adjustment_model: append-only factor series; never rewrite prior observations
proposed_model.reconstruction: raw observation plus all applicable factors as of the query knowledge time

invariants: Adjustment history is immutable and append-only; corrections are new revisions.
Adjusted and raw series are both reproducible from recorded factors.
No factor may be applied before its ex_date_ns.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Reconstructed series match recorded digests before and after each proposed action in the example universe.
Missing or ambiguous factors fail closed.

p2_items.title: Exchange calendars, holidays and sessions
p2_items.problem: Session boundaries and holidays must be explicit, versioned and timezone-safe before any time-series alignment is claimable.
invariants: Each (exchange, trading_date, session_type) has at most one effective definition.
Holidays are explicit records, not inferred from an absence of data.
All instants are stored in UTC nanoseconds with the source timezone retained.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Every example-universe observation maps to exactly one effective session.
Calendar conflicts fail closed.

p2_items.title: Effective time versus observation and knowledge time
p2_items.problem: Using an effective timestamp as if it were known at that time permits look-ahead in point-in-time research.

time_axes.event_effective_ns: when the event is stated to take effect
time_axes.source_published_ns: when the authority published the record
time_axes.observed_ns: when this workspace first captured the record
time_axes.knowledge_available_ns: earliest instant at which the record may be used
time_axes.recorded_ns: when the record was written to the migration store

proposed_model.ordering_rule: knowledge_available_ns >= max(source_published_ns, observed_ns) when those values exist
proposed_model.query_gate: point-in-time queries filter on knowledge_available_ns, never on event_effective_ns alone

invariants: No record is visible to a query whose as-of knowledge time precedes knowledge_available_ns.
Absent publication or observation time fails closed for research use.
Effective and knowledge times are stored in separate named fields.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: A replay with as-of knowledge time immediately before publication returns no record.
No future-knowledge record appears in any proposed point-in-time result.

p2_items.title: Source authority, revisions and correction precedence
p2_items.problem: Multiple revisions and multiple sources require a deterministic precedence rule that never destroys history.

proposed_model.storage: append-only revision chain; superseded revisions retained

invariants: Corrections append a new revision; they never overwrite a prior revision.
Precedence is total and deterministic for any pair of revisions.
A source with UNKNOWN rights cannot outrank an approved authority.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Every conflict in the example universe resolves to one revision by the declared order.
Superseded revisions remain byte-addressable by digest.

p2_items.title: Historical backfill and migration
p2_items.problem: Bulk historical loading must be reproducible, resumable and verifiable before it is trusted for any research claim.

proposed_model.resume_rule: checkpoint_ns plus batch digest defines the only safe resume point

invariants: Each batch is content-addressed; a changed input digest invalidates its checkpoint.
Replay of the example universe at fixed as-of instants is deterministic.
No migration result is accepted before an explicitly approved sign-off.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Dry-run digests match staged-load digests for every batch.
Interrupted migrations resume only from a verified checkpoint.

p2_items.title: Rollback and conflict resolution
p2_items.problem: A bad migration must be reversible without silent overwrites or loss of audit history.

proposed_model.resolution_policy: owner decision required for any conflict that precedence cannot resolve; no silent overwrite

invariants: Rollback restores a prior verified snapshot and records the reason.
Audit log entries are append-only and survive rollback.
Unresolved conflicts fail closed.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: A staged rollback of the example universe restores all prior point-in-time results.
Every injected conflict produces a named, non-silent failure.

p2_items.title: Reference-data rights and retention
p2_items.problem: Reference data can carry redistribution and retention obligations that must be settled before any use.

proposed_model.retention_rule: retention_until_ns must be set before load; revocation moves records to quarantine

invariants: UNKNOWN, REVIEW_PENDING, REFUSED or REVOKED rights block use.
A URL, token or checksum is never rights evidence.
Retention expiry or revocation is enforced by fail-closed quarantine.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: No example-universe record loads without an explicit rights evidence reference.
A simulated revocation quarantines all derived records.

p2_items.title: Point-in-time lookup semantics
p2_items.problem: Point-in-time lookup must combine identity, lifecycle, adjustments, calendar, effective time, knowledge time and precedence into one fail-closed rule.

proposed_model.selection_rule: choose the highest-precedence revision whose effective interval contains as_of_effective_ns and whose knowledge_available_ns <= as_of_knowledge_ns
proposed_model.ambiguity_policy: more than one surviving revision is an error, not an arbitrary pick

invariants: No result uses knowledge unavailable at as_of_knowledge_ns.
Ambiguity, missing interval and missing rights evidence fail closed.
The selected revision is digest-addressable for audit.
acceptance_criteria_proposed: Replay of the example universe at declared as-of instants returns one digest-addressable revision.
Boundary instants on effective and knowledge axes behave identically across both proposed query paths.
